characterization_methods.key_findings: The 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 10 h has a Vickers hardness of 614.4 ± 17.3 HV; the solution-treated baseline is 263.8 ± 1.1 HV.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and value given by the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 19Al alloy after aging at 525 °C for 10 h

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 10 h the phase map is dominated by an α (BCC) matrix with a thin green β-Mn network along the grain boundaries and only minor α-Mn; β-Mn precipitation is 12.1 %.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished with 10 % perchloric acid and 90 % ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify constituent phases and their distribution in the aged 19Al alloy

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 525 °C the α matrix of the 19Al alloy stays almost featureless even after 10 h of aging, consistent with the very slow β-Mn precipitation.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electrolytically polished with 10 % perchloric acid and 90 % ethanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in the aged 19Al alloy

interfaces.interface_notes: For the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C for 10 h the β-Mn precipitates decorate the α grain boundaries; no quantitative interface (coherency/size) data are reported for this specific condition.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (general aging sequence proposed for Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels); for this low-temperature 525 °C/10 h condition the transformation is only at an early stage (12.1% β-Mn).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-19Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated samples aged at temperatures between 525 °C and 650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h, followed by water quenching. This sample corresponds to the 525 °C / 10 h condition.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the hardness given by the average of 5 measurements.
Baseline (parent process proc_st-1100c-10min-oq); Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s, average of 5 measurements.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: elongated, banded lath-like grains with internal streaking (FSD image of the 19Al 525 °C × 10 h condition)

phases_present.morphology: thin network along α grain boundaries; a small amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn within α grains

precipitates.distribution: primarily along α grain boundaries, with a small amount within the α grains

structures.overall_structure: α (BCC) matrix that remains largely untransformed with only a small amount of β-Mn (12.1%) precipitated. β-Mn primarily precipitated along α grain boundaries, with a small amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn also within the α grains.

unmapped_findings: For the 19Al alloy, aging at 525 °C is the mildest aging condition studied: hardness rises only slightly from 562.3 ± 8.9 HV (1 h) to 614.4 ± 17.3 HV (10 h), and the α→β-Mn transformation is far from complete (only 12.1 % β-Mn after 10 h).

The increase in Al content slows the precipitation kinetics of β-Mn during low-temperature aging; at 525 °C only a small amount of β-Mn formed in the 19Al alloy even after 10 h, whereas the 15Al alloy almost completely transformed to β-Mn within 3 h at 525 °C.
The β-Mn primarily precipitated along α grain boundaries, while a small amount of short rod-shaped β-Mn was also observed within the α grains for the 19Al alloy aged at 525 °C.
